cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles (Ezekiel 1:1-3), has a long day ahead. He has just seen a vision of the glory of the LORD and fallen facedown (Ezekiel 1:28). Then the voice speaks: 'Son of man,' He says, 'stand up on your feet and I will speak to you.'

cards.question: As the voice speaks, the Spirit enters Ezekiel and sets him on his feet.

cards.text: Ezekiel's back on his feet, and the LORD gets RIGHT to it with no small talk: 'I am sending you to the Israelites, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me.'

cards.question: The LORD says Israel has been rebelling against Him. Who has been rebelling, and for how long?

answers.text: Them and their fathers to this day
Only them since the exile began
Only their kings for a few years

cards.text: He calls them obstinate and stubborn children, and Ezekiel's opening line is 'This is what the Lord GOD says.' No icebreaker, no joke about the traffic on the way in.

cards.question: Whether Israel listens or refuses to listen, what does the LORD say they will know?

answers.text: That a prophet has been among them
That the exile is ending soon

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Ezekiel not to be afraid, three times in one verse. Friend, when somebody tells me not to be afraid THREE times, that's when I start hopping my gold base toward the exit.

cards.question: The LORD promises Ezekiel that the people around him will be easy to live among.

cards.text: Not even close: he's not to be afraid, though briers and thorns surround him and he dwells among scorpions. Some neighborhood.

cards.question: Even if Israel refuses to listen, the LORD tells Ezekiel to ___ His words to them anyway.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to Ezekiel himself. 'Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house.'

cards.question: Right after telling Ezekiel not to be rebellious, what does the LORD tell him to do?

answers.text: Open his mouth and eat what he's given
Tear his robe and sit in the dust
Go and wash in the River Kebar

cards.text: Eat WHAT, exactly? Ezekiel looks up and sees a hand reaching out to him, holding something.

cards.question: In the hand reaching out to Ezekiel, there's a ___.

cards.text: He unrolls it right in front of Ezekiel, and there's writing on it.

cards.question: The writing on the scroll is only on the front.
The scroll is written on front and back. What kind of words are on it?

cards.text: The LORD is still holding out that scroll of woe. 'Son of man,' He says, 'eat what you find here. Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel.'

cards.question: When the LORD tells him to eat the scroll, Ezekiel opens his mouth and is fed the scroll.

cards.text: And this isn't a nibble, friend. 'Son of man,' He says, 'eat and fill your stomach with this scroll I am giving you.'

cards.question: That scroll is full of lamentation, mourning and woe. How does it taste in Ezekiel's mouth?

cards.text: Then the LORD sends him to the house of Israel, not to a people of unfamiliar speech or difficult language. No translator, no pointing, no saying it LOUDER and SLOWER.

cards.question: The LORD says if He had sent Ezekiel to peoples whose language he couldn't understand, they would have listened to him.

cards.text: True, and that one stings. People who can't understand a word he says would listen, but the LORD says the house of Israel will be unwilling to listen to him.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say the house of Israel won't listen to Ezekiel?

answers.text: Because they won't listen to the LORD
Because Ezekiel is a stranger to them
Because they can't understand his words

cards.text: The LORD says the whole house of Israel is hard-headed and hard-hearted. So He's got a plan for Ezekiel's face.

cards.question: The LORD says He will make Ezekiel's face as ___ as their faces.
The LORD says He will make Ezekiel's forehead like a diamond, harder than flint.

cards.text: Harder than flint, friend, and MY edges went soft from a few years of baking cookies. Then the LORD adds, 'listen carefully to all the words I speak to you, and take them to heart.'

cards.question: Out of the whole house of Israel, which people does the LORD send Ezekiel to speak to?

answers.text: The king of Babylon and his court

cards.text: Then the Spirit lifts Ezekiel up, and behind him comes a great rumbling sound: 'Blessed be the glory of the LORD in His dwelling place!'

cards.question: The rumbling comes from the wings of the living creatures brushing together and the ___ beside them.

cards.text: Wings and wheels, the same living creatures from his vision (Ezekiel 1:5, 1:15). Then the Spirit takes Ezekiel away, with the strong hand of the LORD upon him.

cards.question: As the Spirit carries him off, how does Ezekiel go?

answers.text: In bitterness and anger of spirit

cards.text: He comes to the exiles at Tel-abib, who live by the River Kebar. And the man promised a forehead like a diamond just sits right where they sit.

cards.question: Ezekiel stays there among the exiles, overwhelmed, for ___ days.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave him for now, friend, because the LORD isn't finished with Ezekiel yet.

findings.problem: "has a long day ahead" adds a time frame the text never gives. The passage itself goes on to cover seven days (Ezekiel 3:15), and no verse says the call fits in one day.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "Ezekiel's opening line is 'This is what the Lord GOD says.'" renames what the text calls it. Ezekiel 2:4 says "you are to say to them". It never calls it an opening line or says it comes first.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Story card 5 already tells the baker that Ezekiel is to say "This is what the Lord GOD says" to the Israelites. That gives away the answer "speak" before the fill in the blank asks it, so the card tests nothing.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Because they can't understand his words" is already ruled out. Story card 5 says Ezekiel is sent to the house of Israel, not to a people of unfamiliar speech or difficult language, and story card 7 repeats that contrast.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "MY edges went soft from a few years of baking cookies" changes his backstory. The backstory says "Years of good baking" wore him down, over birthdays, holidays and cutters added one at a time. "A few years" adds a new detail that shrinks that history.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The question frames the answer as "Out of the whole house of Israel". That framing rules out the wrong answer "The king of Babylon and his court", who is not part of the house of Israel. It also adds a selection link between Ezekiel 3:4 and 3:11 that the text does not state.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The living creatures appear for the first time in this lesson on this choice card, with no word on who they are. They are only explained afterward, on story card 16.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line is copied from the doc's examples. It opens like the ✅ example ("And that's where we'll leave it for now") and ends with the doc's storyteller example ("the Lord isn't finished with him"), which this walkthrough also already used on stop 1 card 11's neighbor. It needs an original line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Several story cards have no Papa Dorin voice and read as plain summary. Examples: stop 1 cards 11, 13 and 15, and stop 2 cards 14 and 16. The few jokes elsewhere are mild, and the scroll tasting sweet and Ezekiel sitting overwhelmed for seven days give no real laugh beat.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
